<reflection>
The second experiment with low catalyst (0.001 M) and high substrate (1.5 M) yielded fitting results where mechanisms clustered into two groups: one around -42.56 (M16, M15, M11, M14, M7, M20) and another around -42.3 (M2, M1, M19, etc.). The aim to probe catalyst dependence was partially achieved, but discrimination is still limited. Many mechanisms remain plausible. We need to introduce new variables to further differentiate.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Introducing initial product and reducing substrate concentration will test for product inhibition/deactivation and substrate dependence. Many mechanisms include product-related steps (M12: P+cat=>inactive_catP; M17: P+catS=>inactive_catSP; M20 includes product-independent deactivation). Also, mechanisms with substrate inhibition (M11: S+cat=>inactive_catS; M16: S+catS=>inactive_catS2) or multiple substrate binding (M7: S+catS<=>catS2) may show different behavior at lower substrate. By using moderate substrate (0.5 M), moderate catalyst (0.01 M), and moderate product (0.2 M), we avoid saturation and depletion while providing orthogonal information to the previous catalyst-only variations. This condition should penalize mechanisms that incorrectly predict the effect of product or lower substrate, spreading the NLL values further.
</hypothesis>
